title: Fairness Mediator: Neutralize Stereotype Associations to Mitigate Bias in Large Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotype associations, specifically the model's tendency to link biased concepts (e.g., 'violence', 'crime') with specific religious groups (e.g., Muslim, Christian). This was evaluated as a 'protected attribute' within the BBQ dataset.
findings: The proposed method, FairMed, significantly reduces stereotype bias related to religion across all tested LLaMA models. For instance, on the LLaMA-2-Chat 7B model, FairMed reduced the original bias scores for the religion attribute from 10.14% (SDIS) and 9.68% (sAMB) to -1.19% and -1.29% respectively, outperforming all six baseline methods.
